body:
Records the **candidate, unrefereed claim C₈₉ᵦ < 0.001648970526***, on top of #277, and updates the README bound and recent progress. This replaces the 0.001653032 threshold from this PR's earlier round-3 version; the earlier exact rows are retained. The K5 lower-bound row is unchanged, and no round-4 lower-bound material is released.

Builds on Jeetu SK's [SK2026] construction in #277, the Cayley graph constructions of Parczyk, Pokutta, Spiegel and Szabó, and the folded-Hamming construction ideas of Thomason: #277's page should merge first. Kiem–Pokutta–Spiegel are credited for their flag-algebra methodology and numerical lower-bound discussion; their floating-point estimate is not an upper-bound competitor or an exact certificate. Round 4 uses a 256-part binary Cayley step graphon with probabilities 0, 2648/4041 and 1. Its exact density is **15058298592194934908767847/9131939205947984819238469632 < 0.001648970526**. The decimal is rounded upward; the exact fraction is the certificate value.

Noam Feinstein announced **c5 < 0.001652** at a [Technion seminar on 21 January 2026](https://math.technion.ac.il/events/noam-feinstein/); the [RSA 2025 abstract](https://dmg.tuwien.ac.at/rsa2025/) credits joint work with **Chaim Even-Zohar**. This is an announcement with no public certificate we could check. Its displayed threshold is stronger than our round-3 0.001653032 and weaker than this round. The proposed page has no announcement history rows, so the announcement and comparison are included in Additional comments and the references. No priority or optimality is claimed.

[Construction, proof, certificate, exact counters, controls, receipts and reproduction notes](https://github.com/rpinho/math-certificates/tree/1d38853f31112da873c632fb3d3bd05519eb832a/c89b/round4). The two exact counters are **separately written (same agent)**: a generic full-matrix counter and a root-fixed Cayley counter, both using exact integer arithmetic and GMP. Both were rebuilt and rerun on this package; they agree on the fraction and separately on red and blue totals, with the expected factor of 256. All 36 literal comparisons, ten malformed-input rejections and both false-threshold rejections pass. The selected compressed certificate is byte-identical to the frozen witness. Reproduction requires Python >= 3.10, C++17 and GMP. The inherited credit remains explicit: all 18,528 block-pair densities were optimization variables in #277; Carlos Toledo's [public replay comment](https://github.com/teorth/optimizationproblems/pull/277#issuecomment-6433758020) reports an independent exact replay and 1,248 changed entries in the rounded witness.

[Two AI reviews](https://github.com/rpinho/math-certificates/blob/1d38853f31112da873c632fb3d3bd05519eb832a/c89b/round4/review/README.md), by **Claude Opus 5.5 via Claude Science** and **GPT-6 Astra**, found no false proof step and returned **FLAG for presentation, wording or credit**. The release incorporates their requested corrections, including upward decimal rounding and the Feinstein–Even-Zohar announcement. Astra reran the supplied counters and controls and wrote an additional count; Claude Science used its own exact polynomial and direct CRT counts, but could not refresh live priority sources. A fresh release audit read the proposed 89b page, all open C89 PRs, and public literature/repositories. No further public K5 upper value stronger than this candidate was located in this bounded search. These are AI reviews. **There is no human referee.** The result remains a candidate and unrefereed, and the asterisk stays.

**AI use and author review:** The result, proof, certificate, verification code and submission text were **written and checked by AI agents under Ricardo Pinho's direction**. The exact counters were separately written by the same agent. Ricardo Pinho's direction does not imply line-by-line human verification; none is claimed.

**Verification level: L0** under the strict rule for now: the exact finite certificate also has a complete recount written by a different model, but the receipt-backed packet the strict rule requires for a higher level is not attached yet; the transfer to the bound is standard and cited (definitions: https://github.com/rpinho/math-certificates/blob/59eeb7097f806da05187b5f234445be3589204d4/VERIFICATION_LEVELS.md).

**Models:** GPT-6.1 Sol via Codex (search, construction, exact counters, packaging); Claude Opus 5.5 via Claude Science and GPT-6 Astra (reviews); Claude Code with Claude Opus 5.5 (coordination and this PR text).
